COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.lawCode: Add Art 8-A §§204 - 209, Ec Dev L; rpld §16-j, UDC Act
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4435

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the economic development law, in relation to creating
the New York state strategic training alliance program and to repeal
certain provisions of the urban development corporation act relating
thereto


 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :
This bill creates within the Department of Economic Development the
Strategic Training Alliance Program to fund regional skills training
programs. The purpose of this legislation is to provide the framework
for New York State to meet its current and future workforce needs.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
§ 1- Amends the Economic Development Law by adding a new Article 8-A.

Creates the New York State Strategic Training Alliance Program within
the purview of the Department of Economic Development. It proposes to
deliver skills training services to strategic alliances, which are
defined as networks, associations or other groups of employers within
a training area, joined formally or informally for purposes of solving
common problems or working cooperatively.

For the purposes of this bill, training providers are defined as
community colleges, agricultural and technical colleges, institutions
of higher education, local education agencies, community based
organizations or strategic alliances. Training areas are defined as
geographic areas identified as service delivery areas pursuant to the
Job Training Partnership Act or workforce investment areas pursuant to
the Workforce Investment Act.

The Department of Economic Development, in cooperation with the UDC,
SUNY, CUNY, SED, DOL and any other appropriate State agency, is
required to provide assistance to support training activities by
eligible applicants who are defined as a strategic alliance, or a
consortia of alliances, or a private industry council, or a consortia
of councils acting on behalf of one or more strategic alliances.  The
Department of Economic Development is required to:

-Notify eligible applicants of the availability of funds;
-Solicit and accept plans for training from alliances or PICS on
behalf of alliances;
-Promote the program to the business sector;
- Ensure that 50% or more of program funds are used to assist small
businesses of under 100 employees;
- Ensure that 25% of funds are used to train individuals who are
unemployed, economically disadvantaged or economically dislocated.
The bill also requires applicants to submit plans that include the
following:

-A description of the economy of the training area, highlighting
sectors of growth or job loss;
-A statement of need for assistance and an identification of other
sources of training funds within the area;
-A statement of demand for training by occupation;
-A commitment by the alliance to provide 50% match in the form of cash
or inkind contributions;
-The estimated number of individuals to be trained, hired and retained
as a result of specific projects developed by businesses in the area;
-A description of any high-tech system to be used to disseminate
training in partnership with institutions of higher learning;
-A description of training projects to be supported in the area.  Any
positions created as a result of this training program will be filled
by unemployed, economically disadvantaged or dislocated persons. In
addition, funds will be made available by the department to solicit
proposals to design and develop systems for the implementation of an
electronically supported system for statewide or regional application.
Also, any incumbent worker training proposed to be funded with
discretionary Workforce Investment Act funds must conform to the
provisions of this act.

Annual reports are required to be submitted by the eligible applicants
to the Department of Economic Development and by the department to the
Governor and Legislature. An independent biennial evaluation is also
required of the department.

§ 2- Repeals § 16-j of § 1 of Chapter 174 of the Laws of 1968,
constituting the Urban Development Corporation Act.

§ 3- Effective date.

 EFFECTS OF PRESENT LAW THIS BILL WOULD ALTER :
This bill adds a new article 8-A to the Economic Development Law.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The issue of workforce development and skills training has skyrocketed
to the top of the list of critical economic development issues. In
sector after sector, there are reports of shortages of qualified
workers. This phenomenon will likely increase unless we act quickly to
address it.

In a recent business Week survey, CEOs identified access to a skilled
workforce as the second most important factor in choosing a business
location. During the 90' s, identifying and maintaining the skills of
the workforce has become one of the most important competitive issues
for businesses and the public sector. In the years to come the
competitive pressures of a globalization will only increase the
importance of maintaining a skilled workforce.

The training services envisioned in this bill would be delivered
through strategic alliances, or networks, or consortia of businesses
within an industry. Each alliance would shape the training and choose
the provider. As a result, workers would have the advantage of being
trained to work in any number of firms within an alliance, not just
one. In addition, businesses within an alliance would be ensured of a
pool of skilled workers in reserve.

This innovative approach to skills training and workforce education
can set us on a new path toward making and keeping New York State home
to the very best workforce in the world and, thus, have a major impact
on the competitiveness of New York State's economy well into the new
millenium.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-2008: A.3119
2005-2006: A.3192
2003-2004: A.3364
2001-2002: A.1002
1999-2000: A.7253

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Minimal to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
